ui.capabilities: What this machine is good for
ui.generated_by: Generated by Innards — the report stays on your machine.

verdict.great: Nothing needs your attention. This machine is in good shape.
verdict.fine: No emergencies, but {warnings} thing(s) are costing you performance or reliability.
verdict.attention: One issue needs attention soon, plus {warnings} smaller one(s).
verdict.urgent: {critical} issues need attention now, plus {warnings} smaller one(s).

memory.no_swap.title: No swap configured
memory.no_swap.plain: Your computer has {total} of memory and no backup space on disk. When memory runs out, the system has no choice but to close programs abruptly.
memory.no_swap.informed: There is no swap space at all. With {total} RAM and {available_pct}% currently free, a memory spike will trigger the out-of-memory killer instead of slowing down gracefully.
memory.no_swap.expert: swap_total = 0. Available memory is {available_pct}% of {total}. Without swap the kernel cannot reclaim anonymous pages under pressure, so the OOM killer fires on the first sustained spike. zram is the low-cost fix; a swapfile as a second tier prevents hard kills.
memory.no_swap.action: Add swap: a compressed zram device plus a modest swapfile is safe on any SSD.

memory.swap_ok.title: Swap is configured
memory.swap_ok.plain: Your computer has {swap} of backup memory space, so it won't crash the moment memory runs out.
memory.swap_ok.informed: {swap} of swap is available ({backends}). Memory spikes will slow things down rather than kill programs.

memory.low_available.title: Memory is nearly full
memory.low_available.plain: Only {available} of memory is free right now ({available_pct}%). Things may become sluggish or programs may close unexpectedly.
memory.low_available.informed: Available memory is down to {available} ({available_pct}%). Close what you don't need, or look at what's using it below.
memory.low_available.expert: MemAvailable = {available} ({available_pct}% of total). Reclaimable cache is already counted; this is real pressure.
memory.low_available.action: Close unused apps; check the top memory consumers.

memory.tmpfs_heavy.title: Temporary files are eating memory
memory.tmpfs_heavy.plain: {tmpfs} of your memory is being used by temporary files that live in RAM instead of on disk.
memory.tmpfs_heavy.informed: Temporary filesystems (/tmp, /dev/shm) hold {tmpfs} — {pct}% of RAM. Large files left there are memory, not disk.
memory.tmpfs_heavy.expert: tmpfs usage = {tmpfs} ({pct}% of MemTotal) across /tmp, /dev/shm, /run/user. Large scratch files should go to a disk-backed path or TMPDIR.
memory.tmpfs_heavy.action: Move or delete large files in /tmp.

memory.hog.title: One program is using a lot of memory
memory.hog.plain: {process} is using {rss} — about {pct}% of all your memory.
memory.hog.informed: {process} holds {rss} ({pct}% of RAM). If that's unexpected, restarting it will free it.

memory.small_total.title: Limited memory
memory.small_total.plain: This computer has {total} GB of memory, which is on the small side for today's software.
memory.small_total.informed: {total} GB RAM is below what modern browsers and dev tools comfortably need (8–16 GB).
memory.small_total.action: Add RAM if the machine allows it; otherwise keep fewer things open.

memory.soldered.title: Memory cannot be upgraded
memory.soldered.plain: The {total} GB of memory is built into the board, so it can't be increased later.
memory.soldered.informed: {total} GB {kind} is soldered. Whatever you have now is the ceiling for this machine.
memory.soldered.expert: DMI form factor: row-of-chips ({kind}, {total} GiB). No SODIMM slots.

memory.upgradeable.title: Memory can be upgraded
memory.upgradeable.plain: This computer's memory ({total} GB) can be increased by adding or replacing modules.
memory.upgradeable.informed: {total} GB across {modules} module(s), in slots. Adding RAM is the cheapest big upgrade.

storage.root_nearly_full.title: System drive is {used_pct}% full
storage.root_nearly_full.plain: The main drive has only {free} free. When it fills up, the computer can misbehave or fail to update.
storage.root_nearly_full.informed: {mount} is {used_pct}% used ({free} of {total} free). Below ~10% free, SSDs slow down and updates can fail.
storage.root_nearly_full.expert: {mount}: {used_pct}% used, {free} free. SSD write amplification rises sharply past ~90%; package managers need headroom.
storage.root_nearly_full.action: Free at least 10–15% of the drive.

storage.fs_nearly_full.title: {mount} is {used_pct}% full
storage.fs_nearly_full.plain: The drive at {mount} has only {free} free.
storage.fs_nearly_full.informed: {mount} is {used_pct}% used ({free} of {total} free). Writes to a nearly full drive get slow.
storage.fs_nearly_full.action: Free space or move data elsewhere.

storage.system_hdd.title: System runs on a spinning hard drive
storage.system_hdd.plain: The computer starts and loads programs from an old-style spinning disk ({model}, {size}). This is the single biggest thing slowing it down.
storage.system_hdd.informed: The OS is on an HDD ({model}, {size}). Replacing it with an SSD makes everything feel 3–10× faster — the best upgrade money can buy.
storage.system_hdd.expert: System disk {model} ({size}) is rotational. Random 4K IOPS ~100 vs ~50k+ on any SSD.
storage.system_hdd.action: Replace with an SSD and clone or reinstall.

storage.system_nvme.title: Fast NVMe system drive
storage.system_nvme.plain: The main drive ({model}, {size}) is the fast modern kind.
storage.system_nvme.informed: {model} ({size}) on NVMe {link}. Storage is not your bottleneck.

storage.system_ssd.title: SSD system drive
storage.system_ssd.plain: The main drive ({model}, {size}) is a solid-state drive — good.
storage.system_ssd.informed: {model} ({size}) is a SATA SSD. Fine for everything but the heaviest I/O work.

storage.system_emmc.title: eMMC system storage
storage.system_emmc.plain: The main storage ({size}) is the slow, built-in kind found in budget laptops.
storage.system_emmc.informed: {size} eMMC is soldered, slow, and usually not replaceable.

storage.hot_now.title: {model} is running hot
storage.hot_now.plain: One of your drives is at {temp}°C right now, which is hotter than it should be.
storage.hot_now.informed: {model} is at {temp}°C. Sustained heat shortens SSD life and can cause throttling or dropouts.
storage.hot_now.action: Improve airflow or add a thermal pad.

storage.smart_failing.title: {model} reports it is failing
storage.smart_failing.plain: One of your drives says it is about to fail. Back up your data today.
storage.smart_failing.informed: {model} SMART status is FAILED. Back up now and replace it.
storage.smart_failing.action: Back up immediately and replace the drive.

storage.media_errors.title: {model} has {count} bad sectors
storage.media_errors.plain: One of your drives has started developing damaged areas. Back up anything important.
storage.media_errors.informed: {model} reports {count} media/reallocated/pending sector(s). This usually gets worse.
storage.media_errors.expert: Media errors + reallocated + pending = {count}. Any non-zero value is a replace-soon signal.
storage.media_errors.action: Back up, then replace the drive.

storage.unsafe_shutdowns.title: {model} sees many unclean shutdowns
storage.unsafe_shutdowns.plain: This drive has been switched off without warning {unsafe} times — roughly one in every {pct}% of power-ups. That's a sign of crashes, hangs, or power loss.
storage.unsafe_shutdowns.informed: {unsafe} unsafe shutdowns out of {cycles} power cycles ({pct}%). Either the machine is hanging on reboot, or power is being cut.
storage.unsafe_shutdowns.expert: unsafe_shutdowns={unsafe}, power_cycles={cycles} ({pct}%). On DRAM-less NVMe drives with HMB this often indicates the controller failing to exit deep APST states at shutdown; consider nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us=0.
storage.unsafe_shutdowns.action: Check for reboot hangs; consider disabling NVMe deep power states.

storage.critical_temp_history.title: {model} has overheated in the past
storage.critical_temp_history.plain: This drive has spent {minutes} minutes above its danger temperature over its life. It probably needs better cooling.
storage.critical_temp_history.informed: {minutes} min at critical temperature and {warning_minutes} min above warning. The drive is protecting itself by slowing down when hot.
storage.critical_temp_history.expert: critical_comp_time={minutes}m, warning_temp_time={warning_minutes}m. Sustained >critical triggers thermal throttling and accelerates NAND wear.
storage.critical_temp_history.action: Add a thermal pad, clean fans, or check for a blocked M.2 bay.

storage.wear_high.title: {model} is {used_pct}% worn
storage.wear_high.plain: This drive has used up {used_pct}% of its rated lifetime.
storage.wear_high.informed: SSD wear is at {used_pct}%. Past 80%, plan a replacement.
storage.wear_high.action: Plan a replacement; keep backups current.

storage.wear_low.title: {model} has plenty of life left
storage.wear_low.plain: The main drive has used only {used_pct}% of its rated lifetime.
storage.wear_low.informed: {used_pct}% wear after {written} written and {hours} hours on.

storage.smart_unavailable.title: Drive health could not be read
storage.smart_unavailable.plain: Innards couldn't check the health of your drives. Running it with administrator rights, or installing smartmontools, enables this.
storage.smart_unavailable.informed: SMART data was unavailable (needs smartmontools and usually elevated rights).
storage.smart_unavailable.expert: No smartctl/nvme-cli output for any device.
storage.smart_unavailable.action: Install smartmontools and rerun with elevated rights.

cpu.old.title: Processor is about {age} years old
cpu.old.plain: The {brand} came out around {year}. It still works, but newer chips do the same work in a fraction of the time and power.
cpu.old.informed: {brand} (~{year}). A current mid-range CPU is roughly 2–4× faster per core and has 3–4× the cores.

cpu.modern.title: Modern processor
cpu.modern.plain: The {brand} is recent ({year}) and not holding you back.

cpu.few_cores.title: Only {cores} CPU cores
cpu.few_cores.plain: This processor has {cores} cores. Heavy tasks that split across many cores will feel slow.
cpu.few_cores.informed: {cores} cores / {threads} threads. Fine for everyday use; compiles, video and container stacks will be CPU-bound.

cpu.hot.title: Processor is running at {temp}°C
cpu.hot.plain: The processor is very hot right now. It's slowing itself down to stay safe, which makes everything feel slower.
cpu.hot.informed: {temp}°C with {throttle_events} throttle events logged. Dust, dried thermal paste, or a blocked vent are the usual causes.
cpu.hot.action: Clean fans and vents; consider repasting.

cpu.no_avx2.title: No AVX2 support
cpu.no_avx2.plain: This processor lacks an instruction set that a lot of modern software (especially AI tools) expects.
cpu.no_avx2.informed: {brand} has no AVX2. Some builds of ML/AI software and video codecs won't run or will be very slow.

thermal.fan_high_at_idle.title: Fan is loud while the machine is mostly idle
thermal.fan_high_at_idle.plain: The fan is spinning at {rpm} RPM even though the computer isn't doing much. Something is keeping it warm.
thermal.fan_high_at_idle.informed: Fan at {rpm} RPM, CPU {temp}°C at low load. Check for a background process, dust, or degraded thermal paste.
thermal.fan_high_at_idle.expert: fan={rpm} rpm, cpu={temp}°C, load below 50% of cores.

battery.worn.title: Battery holds {health}% of its original capacity
battery.worn.plain: The battery has worn down: it now holds {full_wh} Wh of the {design_wh} Wh it was built with, after {cycles} charge cycles. Expect short runtimes.
battery.worn.informed: {health}% health, {cycles} cycles. Below ~60% a replacement is worth it if you use it unplugged.
battery.worn.action: Replace the battery if portability matters.

battery.ok.title: Battery is healthy ({health}%)
battery.ok.plain: The battery holds {health}% of its original capacity after {cycles} cycles.

gpu.discrete.title: Dedicated graphics: {name}
gpu.discrete.plain: This computer has its own graphics card ({name}), so games, video and AI tools have real horsepower.
gpu.discrete.informed: {name} {vram}. Dedicated GPU available for games, encoding, and local AI.

gpu.integrated_only.title: Graphics are built into the processor
gpu.integrated_only.plain: Graphics come from the processor itself ({name}). Fine for video and desktop work; not for modern games or AI training.
gpu.integrated_only.informed: Integrated {name}. Hardware video decode works; GPU compute and gaming are out of reach.

network.wifi_only.title: Wi-Fi only, no wired port
network.wifi_only.plain: This computer connects only over Wi-Fi. For big transfers or server duties, a wired adapter helps.
network.wifi_only.informed: No Ethernet interface detected. A USB-C or Thunderbolt Ethernet adapter gives you stable gigabit.

network.ethernet_slow.title: Wired link is only {mbps} Mbit/s
network.ethernet_slow.plain: The network cable connection is running slower than it should — check the cable or the switch port.
network.ethernet_slow.informed: {iface} negotiated {mbps} Mbit/s. Usually a bad cable or an old switch.

system.high_load.title: System is under heavy load
system.high_load.plain: The computer is working harder than it can keep up with right now.
system.high_load.informed: 5-minute load average {load} on {cpus} CPUs. Something is saturating the processor.

system.io_wait_high.title: Waiting on disks {io_wait}% of the time
system.io_wait_high.plain: A large part of the time, the processor is just waiting for a disk to respond.
system.io_wait_high.informed: I/O wait is {io_wait}%. A slow or busy drive (often USB) is holding everything else up.

system.vm.title: Running in a virtual machine
system.vm.plain: This is a virtual computer; hardware details reflect what the host allows it to see.
system.vm.informed: VM detected. Battery, thermal and SMART data are not meaningful here.

system.uptime_long.title: Up for {days} days
system.uptime_long.plain: The computer hasn't restarted in {days} days. Updates that need a restart are probably waiting.
system.uptime_long.informed: {days} days uptime. Kernel/firmware updates need a reboot to apply.

rec.add_swap.title: Add swap (free)
rec.add_swap.body: Set up a compressed zram swap plus a swapfile. On Linux this is two packages; on Windows and macOS make sure the pagefile/swap is enabled.
rec.add_swap.why: Without swap, running out of memory kills programs instead of slowing down.

rec.free_space.title: Free up the system drive (free)
rec.free_space.body: The system drive is {used_pct}% full with {free} left. Clear caches, old downloads, and unused apps.
rec.free_space.why: SSDs slow down and updates fail when nearly full.

rec.tmpfs_to_disk.title: Move temporary files off RAM (free)
rec.tmpfs_to_disk.body: {tmpfs} of temporary files are sitting in memory. Move large scratch files to a disk path.
rec.tmpfs_to_disk.why: Every byte in /tmp is memory your programs can't use.

rec.ssd_replace_failing.title: Replace the failing drive
rec.ssd_replace_failing.body: {model} ({size}) is showing failure signs. Replace it with a {target_gb} GB {interface} SSD and restore from backup.
rec.ssd_replace_failing.why: A failing drive will eventually take your data with it.

rec.ssd_replace_hdd.title: Replace the hard drive with an SSD
rec.ssd_replace_hdd.body: Swap the {size} spinning drive for a {target_gb} GB {interface} SSD. Clone it or reinstall.
rec.ssd_replace_hdd.why: The single most noticeable upgrade possible: everything opens 3–10× faster.

rec.ssd_bigger.title: Move to a bigger SSD
rec.ssd_bigger.why: You've said storage is a pain point, and this drive is on the small side.

rec.ram_add.title: Add memory: {have} GB → {target} GB
rec.ram_add.why: Your chosen workloads want at least {target} GB to run comfortably.

rec.ram_add_check.title: Add memory: {have} GB → {target} GB (check slots first)
rec.ram_add_check.body: Innards couldn't confirm whether this machine has memory slots. Check the model's service manual, then install {kind} modules to reach {target} GB.
rec.ram_add_check.why: Your chosen workloads want at least {target} GB to run comfortably.

rec.ram_soldered.title: Memory is the ceiling — and it's soldered
rec.ram_soldered.body: You have {have} GB and your workloads want {target} GB, but this machine's memory can't be upgraded.
rec.ram_soldered.why: This is the strongest reason to consider a different machine, not a part.

rec.battery_replace.title: Replace the battery
rec.battery_replace.body: Health is {health}%. A replacement for the {model} is usually a 10-minute job with a screwdriver.
rec.battery_replace.why: You said you use it unplugged; this is the cheapest way to get hours back.

rec.thermal_service.title: Clean and repaste
rec.thermal_service.body: Blow out the fans, replace the thermal paste, and add a thermal pad to the SSD if it's exposed. CPU is at {cpu_temp}°C.
rec.thermal_service.why: Heat is making the machine throttle and louder than it needs to be.

rec.gpu_laptop_no_slot.title: GPU work needs a different machine
rec.gpu_laptop_no_slot.body: This laptop has no dedicated GPU and can't take one. For gaming or AI work, consider a desktop, a machine with a discrete GPU, or renting GPU time.
rec.gpu_laptop_no_slot.why: No upgrade path exists for graphics on this chassis.

rec.gpu_add.title: Add a graphics card ({vram} GB)
rec.gpu_add.body: A mid-range card with {vram} GB of VRAM unlocks gaming, video encoding, and local AI on this desktop.
rec.gpu_add.why: Your workloads are GPU-bound and this machine has a slot.

rec.machine_replace.title: Plan a replacement machine
rec.machine_replace.body: This {age}-year-old machine ({cores_now} cores, {ram_now} GB) can't reach what you need. Look for at least {target_cores} cores and {target_ram} GB RAM ({form}).
rec.machine_replace.why: Several of your workloads score poorly and the limiting parts can't be upgraded.

rec.keep.title: Keep it — nothing to buy
rec.keep.body: Your workloads are well served by this machine. The free fixes above are all that's worth doing.
rec.keep.why: Spending money here wouldn't change your day-to-day.

advisor.budget: What would you be willing to spend?
advisor.portability: Do you need to use it away from a desk?
